description: Structured frame sizing rules mapping face measurements to recommended frame dimensions. Supports Optiwar's MediaPipe face measurement and virtual try-on system.

face_width_mm.description: Total face width measured at the widest point (temple to temple across cheekbones)
face_width_mm.measurement_method: Use Optiwar's face measurement tool at /tryon or measure with a ruler from the front of one temple to the other at the widest point of your face

pd_mm.description: Pupillary Distance — distance between the centres of both pupils
pd_mm.measurement_method: Use Optiwar's /tryon tool, ask your optometrist, or self-measure in a mirror at 20cm distance

fields.lens_width: Horizontal width of one lens in mm (typically 44-58mm). Larger = wider frame.
fields.bridge_width: Distance between the two lenses at the nose (typically 15-22mm). Larger = wider nose fit.
fields.temple_length: Length of the arm from hinge to ear tip (typically 135-150mm). Most adults fit 140mm.

face_width_to_frame.notes: Look for frames labelled Narrow or Small. Optiwar frame sizes starting with 46-xx or 48-xx.
Medium-narrow fit. Most Optiwar frames in 49-18 or 50-18 range.
Standard/average fit. Widest selection of Optiwar frames available (52-18-140 is the most common size).
Medium-wide fit. Look for larger frames, typically 54-xx or 55-xx lens width.
Wide fit. Limited selection — look for wide/large labelled frames. Consider adjustable nose pads for better fit.

pd_to_bridge.notes: Narrow PD — narrow bridge keeps lenses centred on pupils
Average PD — standard bridge width works well
Wide PD — wider bridge ensures proper optical centering

face_shape_to_frame_style.description: Balanced proportions, slightly wider at cheekbones
face_shape_to_frame_style.notes: Oval faces suit most frame shapes. Avoid frames that are too large or too small for your face width.

face_shape_to_frame_style.description: Equal width and length, soft angles, full cheeks
face_shape_to_frame_style.notes: Angular frames add definition and contrast to round features. Avoid round frames that echo face shape.

face_shape_to_frame_style.description: Strong jawline, equal width forehead and jaw, angular features
face_shape_to_frame_style.notes: Curved and round frames soften angular features. Avoid angular frames that emphasise squareness.

face_shape_to_frame_style.description: Wider forehead, narrower chin, prominent cheekbones
face_shape_to_frame_style.notes: Light, thin frames or rimless balance the wider forehead. Avoid heavy top-bar styles (Clubmaster) that widen the upper face.

face_shape_to_frame_style.description: Longer than wide, straight cheek line
face_shape_to_frame_style.notes: Wider frames with strong horizontal lines add width. Deep lenses break up face length.

fit_formula.description: Calculate approximate total frame width from face width
fit_formula.optical_center: lens_width + bridge_width should approximately equal PD for optimal optical centering

example.calculation: Face width 137mm → frame width ~135-140mm. PD 66.5 → lens 52 + bridge 18 = 70 (close to PD + bridge overlap). Recommended: 52-18-140 frames.
